speaker: Leonard
text: Sheldon, I am so sorry I dragged you through this. And you were right about my motives. I was hoping to establish a relationship with Penny that might have someday led to sex.

speaker: Sheldon
text: It's okay. It wasn't my first pantsing, and it won't be my last. Well, you got me out of my pants.

speaker: Leonard
text: Anyway, I've learned my lesson. She's out of my league. I'm done with her. I've got my work. One day I'll win the Nobel Prize, and then I'll die alone.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Don't think like that. You're not going to die alone.

speaker: Leonard
text: Thank you, Sheldon. You're a good friend.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You're certainly not going to win a Nobel Prize.

speaker: Howard
text: This is one of my favorite places to kick back after a quest. They have a great house ale. Yeah, I've had him since level 10. His name is Buttons. Anyway, if you had your own game character, we could hang out, maybe go on a quest.

speaker: Penny
text: Wow, cool tiger. Uh, sounds interesting. Oh, I don't think I'll be able to stop thinking about it.

speaker: Howard
text: So you'll think about it.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Smooth.

speaker: Leonard
text: We're home.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, oh my god, what happened?

speaker: Leonard
text: Well, your ex-boyfriend sends his regards, and I think the rest is fairly self-explanatory.

speaker: Penny
text: I'm so sorry. I really thought if you guys went instead of me, you wouldn't be such an ass.

speaker: Leonard
text: No, that was a valid hypothesis.

speaker: Sheldon
text: That was a valid hypo- what is happening to you?

speaker: Penny
text: Really, thank you so much for going and trying. You just, ugh, you're so terrific. Really. Why don't you put some clothes on? I'll get my purse, and dinner is on me, okay?

speaker: Leonard
text: Really great.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Thank you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You're not done with her, are you?

speaker: Leonard
text: Our babies will be smart and beautiful.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Not to mention imaginary.

speaker: Leonard
text: Is Thai food okay with you, Penny?

speaker: Sheldon
text: We can't have Thai food. We had Indian for lunch. They're both curry-based cuisines. They would be gastronomically redundant. I can see we're going to have to spell out everything for this girl.

speaker: Penny
text: Any ideas, Raj?

speaker: Howard
text: Turn left on Lake Street and head up to Colorado. I know a wonderful little sushi bar that has karaoke.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, that sounds like fun.

speaker: Howard
text: Baby, baby, don't get hooked on me.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I don't know what your odds are in the world as a whole, but as far as the population of this car goes, you're a veritable Mac Daddy.
